KSA Luxury Residential · Competitive Intelligence

Six months of luxury residential ads
read against Diriyah.

Diriyah's own paid-media presence sits at five Meta creatives, four of them paused for missing disclaimers, against forty-plus competitor-led creatives advertising Wadi Safar land that Diriyah owns. Six platforms checked. The pattern, in detail, follows.

Section 01 · Overview

The luxury picture, briefly.

Six months of paid advertising across Saudi Arabia's luxury residential segment is a thin object measured in creative count alone, and a denser one measured in voice. Diriyah Company, a developer with a five-hundred-unit residential brief and a portfolio of branded residences from Armani, Aman, Baccarat, Raffles, Chedi, Corinthia, and Ritz-Carlton, ran five Meta creatives in the period. Four of those creatives were paused without ever reaching their audience, halted at the disclaimer review. One ran. By contrast, the partners selling Diriyah-owned Wadi Safar land — a UAE-listed developer, two real-estate brokerages, and the architect-of-record — produced more than forty active creatives between them in the same window, with a clarity of voice and budget that the brand itself did not match.

The numbers below are not a critique of restraint. Diriyah's positioning, ultra-luxury at a deliberately small scale, makes mass paid-media volume the wrong KPI. The numbers are an audit of where the brand's voice carries on the most active platform and where it does not. They are also an audit of where Diriyah has chosen to trade voice for partner reach, and what that trade looks like on the ground.

The matrix that follows reads each developer across six advertising platforms: Meta, Google's Ads Transparency Center, TikTok's Commercial Content Library, X (formerly Twitter), LinkedIn, and Snap. Three of those platforms are not publicly inspectable without authentication or have been deprecated. The report names each gap honestly.

Section 02 · Diriyah-only

What Diriyah Company itself ran.

The Diriyah Company page on Meta ran five distinct creatives between 30 July 2024 and 30 June 2025, and zero new creatives for the eleven months that followed. The single direct sales-driven creative, an Armani Residences spread captioned Live where stories are stitched in stone and style, ran for eight weeks and ended in late June 2025. The four others, all brand and master-plan creatives intended to carry the long-form Diriyah message, were paused for a missing required disclaimer. Two of them had already reached more than one million people and accumulated between 700,000 and one million impressions before the policy review caught them.

The Wadi Safar page itself, scraped under both English (Wadi Safar) and Arabic (وادي صفار) keywords, surfaces only third-party advertising. It does not run a direct page presence. There is no The Wadi Safar Company Meta page operating sales creative.

The honest framing: Diriyah Company has produced one active sales-driven creative in the period, four well-built brand creatives that never went live, and zero direct-page presence on Wadi Safar. Five Meta creatives, six months. The Google Ads Transparency Center returns the diriyahcompany.sa domain but no verified advertiser counts active in Saudi Arabia. TikTok, X, LinkedIn, and Snap return either the platform shell, an authentication wall, or empty bodies — all of which are noted in the matrix above and in the methodology below.

This is the corrected picture. The previous version of this report blended Diriyah-direct creatives with partner-driven activity into a single ecosystem view; that flattened the gap. Here the brand's own output gets its own section. The partner-driven activity around Wadi Safar gets its own section after this one.

Section 03 · Competitors on Diriyah land

Third parties advertising in Wadi Safar territory.

Three companies advertised on Diriyah-owned land in this period without contributing to Diriyah's own brand voice. DarGlobal, a UAE-listed luxury developer trading on the London Stock Exchange, ran sixteen ads with twenty-nine distinct creatives for Rayana Mansions and Amara at Rayana — the largest single residential push in the entire Saudi luxury landscape this period, more than double Red Sea Global's combined output and roughly six times Diriyah's own. Christie's Real Estate Saudi, the local franchise of the Christie's International real-estate arm, ran five ads for Rayana with copy that defines a category Diriyah does not yet define for itself: A new benchmark for living in Riyadh.

Dar Al Omran is the third advertiser, with a single Meta creative for the Wadi Safar Experience Center plus thirty-three verified Google ads under the Rasem Badran brand. Dar Al Omran is the architect-of-record for Diriyah; framing the Experience Center as a story unfolding in the stillness of the valley is, again, a positioning Diriyah's own page has not articulated in the period.

The composite picture is straightforward. Wadi Safar is being marketed actively, with restraint, and at scale. The voice is third-party. The credit is third-party. The buying public is hearing about the most expensive three square kilometres of Saudi real estate from the company that built the masterplan, the broker that sells it, and the architect who designed it. They are not hearing about it from the brand that owns it.

Section 04 · ROSHN luxury orbit

Elie Saab branded villas, broker-led.

ROSHN's mass-market giga-project (Sedra, Marafy, Al Manar, Al Arous, Al Danah, Al Falwah) is out of scope for a luxury benchmark. The luxury orbit around it is not. The Elie Saab branded villas at Sedra are the most aggressively priced luxury creative system in the Saudi market right now, and the entire push is broker-led: Expat Key Real Estate, an English-language broker targeting expat buyers, runs six ads with twelve distinct creatives across the same template at three price points (SAR 200,000 rentals, SAR 1.4M apartments, SAR 3.8M villas), all delivered across Facebook, Instagram, Messenger, and WhatsApp.

The Premium Residency hook — foreign ownership eligible, near King Khaled Airport — is the only sales lever in this benchmark that is built explicitly around the Saudi Premium Residency programme. It is a clean idea. ROSHN itself runs no luxury creative on its own page in the period; the Etoile by Elie Saab international broker test (Victor Sadygov Real Estate) ran for twenty-four hours in September 2025 and went silent.

What this section says about Diriyah: the most disciplined luxury creative system in the Saudi market is not running on a giga-project's own page. It is running on a broker's page, against a programme (Premium Residency) that Diriyah's branded residences are equally eligible for. Diriyah's sixty-thousand-dollar-a-square-metre apartments could carry the same hook, with substantially more architectural narrative.

Section 05 · Red Sea Global luxury orbit

Nammos and Miraval, sales-language only.

Red Sea Global is the most active luxury-residential giga-project on Meta in the period, with the discipline to match. Nammos Residences at AMAALA, a Mykonos-import lifestyle brand that opened sales in April 2026, runs three creatives in tight rotation: ownership-led, service-led, and atmosphere-led. Miraval The Red Sea Residences, the wellness-led residence-and-resort hybrid, runs an evergreen system of six creatives that has been live since December 2025.

The Google Ads Transparency Center returns thirty-seven verified ads under Red Sea Global Company in Saudi Arabia. That is the highest verified Google count of any developer in this benchmark and one of the very few Saudi giga-projects with a clean Google ATC presence. Red Sea Global is one of two developers in this report (the other being Dar Al Omran) running a coordinated Meta and Google strategy.

What this section says about Diriyah: the closest peer in scale, ambition, and price point is Red Sea Global, and it runs five times Diriyah's verified Google volume and three times Diriyah's active Meta volume, with a substantively quieter voice. The Nammos creatives are not loud. The Miraval creatives are not loud. They are present.

Section 06 · Notable absences

Twelve branded-residence operators on permanent silence.

Twelve branded-residence operators with confirmed Saudi projects ran zero direct sales creatives in Saudi Arabia in the period. Aman, Aman Residences (including Amansamar at Wadi Safar), Baccarat, Raffles, Chedi, Corinthia, Ritz-Carlton Reserve, Six Senses, Mandarin Oriental Jeddah Central, Bulgari (under multiple programme rumours), Four Seasons Private Residences (Shura Island), and SLS Shura Marina are silent on Meta in Saudi Arabia.

The interpretation is not that the residences are not selling. It is that they are selling through direct relationship, broker outreach, and global geographies (London, Singapore, Dubai). The Saudi-targeted ad infrastructure for branded ultra-luxury residences does not yet exist. The buyer profile is small enough that paid social is not the right channel.

The structural risk: branded residences sell on the strength of the operator's reputation and the developer's masterplan. If neither side runs the conversation, the conversation runs through brokers (Expat Key, Christie's, Bayut). The brokers, in turn, frame the property in the broker's voice, not the developer's. Wadi Safar is the most extreme version of this in the current market.

Section 07 · Recommendations

Six moves, ranked by impact.

The recommendations below are scoped to the Diriyah luxury segment, on six platforms, over a twelve-month horizon. They are not a creative manifesto. They are the smallest set of moves that close the gap visible in this report.

1. Resolve the disclaimer compliance issue at the Diriyah Company page level.

Four of the five Meta creatives the Diriyah Company page produced in the last twelve months were paused for missing required disclaimers. That is the single biggest paid-media issue identified in this report. It is not a creative problem; it is a Meta Business Manager configuration issue. Resolution is hours of work and recovers an estimated three to four million impressions of brand-investment that have already been paid for and are sitting on inactive creatives.

2. Run a coordinated brand-led Wadi Safar creative in parallel to the partner push, not as a replacement for it.

DarGlobal's twenty-nine creatives for Rayana represent partner energy that is doing the brand a service in absolute reach terms. The risk is voice: the Saudi public is hearing Wadi Safar described as the most exclusive three square kilometres in the world, golf, hotel, members only club by a UAE developer. A Diriyah Company-direct creative on the same platform, in the same period, with the same audience targeting, framing Wadi Safar as the heritage anchor of the larger project, would re-establish editorial control without slowing partner momentum.

3. Open a Google Ads Transparency Center presence with the diriyahcompany.sa domain verified.

Diriyah Company's domain is registered with Google but no verified advertiser count surfaces. This is a process action, not a budget decision. Verified ATC presence in Saudi Arabia matters for two reasons: it gives the brand a public-facing audit trail that buyers can reference, and it removes Diriyah from the small list of luxury developers without one. Red Sea Global has thirty-seven verified Google ads. Dar Al Omran has thirty-three. Diriyah has none visible.

4. Build a per-residence creative system around the Premium Residency hook.

The most disciplined creative system in this report (Expat Key's Elie Saab villas) is built around foreign ownership and Premium Residency eligibility at three price points. Diriyah's branded residences (Armani, Aman, Baccarat, Raffles, Chedi, Corinthia, Ritz-Carlton Reserve) are equally eligible. A creative system that frames each operator at their price point, with the same Premium Residency hook, would give the brand a residence-by-residence drumbeat that does not currently exist. Target: thirty creatives over twelve months, six per operator.

5. Treat TikTok, X, LinkedIn, and Snap as platforms where the absence is currently shared, not lost.

None of the developers in this benchmark are visible on TikTok, X, LinkedIn, or Snap from a public-inspection standpoint. The signal is that the entire Saudi luxury residential segment has not yet built creative for those platforms. The opportunity for Diriyah is not to scale presence on those platforms — it is to be the first developer in this segment with a coherent creative on TikTok specifically, where the buyer skew is younger Saudi HNW and the cost-per-impression is materially lower than Meta. A four-creative TikTok pilot in Q3 2026, geofenced to Riyadh and Jeddah, would close the no-data column in the matrix above.

6. Re-run this benchmark quarterly.

Most of the data in this report is volatile by week. The DarGlobal push for Rayana started in late April 2026 and could plausibly be a launch-window peak. Red Sea Global's Nammos campaign is sales-window-driven and will fade. ROSHN's broker channel is broker-managed and does not move with the giga-project's brand calendar. A quarterly re-scrape, with this same six-platform discipline, gives the marketing function early signal on competitor launches and a structural view of which platforms are warming up. Recommend automating the Meta and Google ATC scrapes via Playwright into a Looker Studio panel.

Section 08 · Methodology

What was measured and how.

Methodology and caveats

  • Meta Ad Library is the primary source. Full read via headless Chromium. Both English and Arabic keyword passes plus advertiser-page filter. Each unique creative tied to one campaign counts as one variant; this ad has multiple versions markers are counted as the stated number. Variant counts have plus or minus fifteen percent uncertainty.
  • Google Ads Transparency Center shows verified-advertiser counts for ads served in Saudi Arabia. Counts are interactive UI scrapes, not API. The diriyahcompany.sa, wadisafar.com, and christiesrealestate.sa domains are registered but produce no verified-advertiser counts, indicating either no current advertiser, no SA-region ads, or unverified accounts.
  • TikTok Commercial Content Library at library.tiktok.com/ads renders an empty body in unauthenticated headless browsers. The library exists, but the SPA does not hydrate without TikTok's cookie set. Marked as not publicly inspectable in the matrix.
  • X (formerly Twitter) Ad Transparency: the Twitter Ad Library product (ads.twitter.com/transparency) was deprecated when X retired the standalone reports. Candidate URLs (ads.x.com/transparency, transparency.x.com) returned empty bodies in our session. Marked as deprecated.
  • LinkedIn Ad Library at linkedin.com/ad-library and the company-level posts feed both require authentication. Marked as gated.
  • Snap Ads Library at snap.com/political-ads exposes political ads only. Commercial advertiser-level inventory is not publicly indexed. Marked as zero across the board.
  • Some channels are not in scope: email, SMS, sales-center walk-ins, broker WhatsApp campaigns, out-of-home billboards, TV, radio, podcasts, and search-engine paid placements outside Google. Several developers are likely heavy spenders on these channels, not visible to this benchmark.
  • Counts are a snapshot. Ad libraries change daily. Same-day re-runs may show plus or minus five to ten percent variation.
